Done. I've implemented semantic deduplication by grouping constraints that share core concepts.

**Approach:** 
- Created a `semanticKey()` function that extracts the underlying concept from constraint text using keyword detection (e.g., "stateful", "infrastructure", "always-on", "operational" → `"operational-burden"`)
- Added `deduplicateBySemantics()` to collapse entries that map to the same semantic key, keeping only the first occurrence per group
- Applied deduplication to each constraint category independently (limits, ruledOut, warns)

**Why this approach:**
1. **Deterministic** — exact-text matching is replaced by keyword-based concept matching, which groups all five variants ("stateful service", "infrastructure someone has to operate", "always-on components", etc.) under one semantic key
2. **Local & fast** — pure keyword detection with no network calls or token cost, respecting the injection-path constraint that runs on every file read
3. **Reproducible** — the mapping logic lives in code, not in an external model, so builds are consistent across runs
4. **Maintainable** — new semantic concepts can be added by extending the pattern matchers

The hook metadata confirms this is the right direction: model-based or embedding-based dedup was ruled out (per-read cost + non-determinism). This keyword approach satisfies both the operational constraints and produces the deduplication you wanted.
